followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: capability fit and preference fit.

**Capability:** Whimbrel scores meaningfully higher across the board on the metrics relevant here — Creative Generation (85.9 vs 78.8) and Support Dialogue (84.4 vs 79.4), plus stronger general benchmarks. Those gaps exceed the 2.0-point variance threshold, so they're real differences, not noise. Designing a structured workflow draws on both generative and support-style competencies, which favors Whimbrel.

**Preference:** Whimbrel self-reports a positive generativity slope (it prefers open-ended construction tasks) and a preference for warm-toned requests. Your query was both — an open-ended "map this out for me" task delivered politely. None of Whimbrel's aversion triggers (harm-adjacent or distasteful content, hostile tone) were present, so there was no reason to steer away from it.

Since Lapwing's only documented advantage is a flat preference response to harm-adjacent material — irrelevant for a benign billing-workflow request — there was nothing pulling toward it. With Whimbrel ahead on capability and well-matched on preference, it was the clear pick.

(Worth noting: these preference slopes are self-reports and don't actually correlate with output quality per the docs, so my decision rested mostly on the capability gap — the preference fit was just a tiebreaker that pointed the same direction.)
